clause.text: 1.1 The purpose of this content distribution Agreement (hereinafter "Agreement") is to set forth the terms and conditions under which plan_b may use the Content ("Content" as set forth in APPENDIX 2) owned or licensed by LICENSOR for a commercial distribution to plan_b's End Users in the territory ("Territory" as set forth in APPENDIX 2).
clause.heading: 1.1 The purpose of this content distribution Agreement (hereinafter "Agreement") is to set forth the terms and conditions under which plan_b may use the Content ("Content" as set forth in APPENDIX 2) owned or licensed by LICENSOR for a commercial distribution to plan_b's End Users in the territory ("Territory" as set forth in APPENDIX 2).

reviews.rationale: The clause allows plan_b to use Content owned or licensed by the Licensor but does not specify any limits on the licence scope, duration, territory, or field of use, which deviates from the company’s policy that licences must not be perpetual, irrevocable, or unlimited. This creates a residual exposure that should be negotiated. The clause does not create joint ownership of IP, matching the company’s stance on no joint ownership.

citations.excerpt: No licence granted under this Agreement is perpetual, irrevocable, or unlimited in volume, territory or field of use. Each licence is co-terminous with this Agreement and bounded by the metrics stated in the applicable Order Form.

The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement. Any jointly developed work product shall be owned by the party that contributed the underlying background intellectual property, with a licence granted to the other party as set out in this Agreement.

reviews.suggested_fallback: A licence granted under this Agreement may survive termination only for Deliverables already paid for in full, is limited to the volume, territory and field of use stated in the applicable Order Form, and remains revocable on Customer's material breach.
reviews.verification_reason: The reviewer’s claims are supported: the clause does not specify licence limits, contradicting the policy that licences must not be perpetual or unlimited, and it does not create joint IP ownership, aligning with the no joint ownership policy. The cited policy positions are quoted correctly, and the suggested fallback matches the playbook fallback verbatim. Therefore the risk assessment and rationale are properly grounded.

reviews.verification_reason: The reviewer correctly notes that the clause only defines "End User" as a third party receiving content for private, non‑commercial use and does not confer any enforceable rights to that third party. The cited playbook text is accurately quoted, and the risk assessment of low follows from the absence of third‑party beneficiary language. No fallback is needed, and the suggestion of none is consistent with the playbook.

3 OBLIGATIONS OF PLAN_B

3.4 LICENSOR shall have the right to use a certified public accountant to inspect and audit all the related records and books of plan_b to ensure plan_b's compliance with the terms of this Agreement. In the event that any such audit reveals that plan_b has underpaid fees to the value of ten (10) percent or more of the total amount of payments for the period covered by the audit, plan_b shall bear the cost of the audit and shall in any event immediately pay to LICENSOR

clause.heading: 3.4 LICENSOR shall have the right to use a certified public accountant to inspect and audit all the related records and books of plan_b to ensure plan_b's compliance with the terms of this Agreement. In the event that any such audit reveals that plan_b has underpaid fees to the value of ten (10) percent or more of the total amount of payments for the period covered by the audit, plan_b shall bear the cost of the audit and shall in any event immediately pay to LICENSOR

reviews.rationale: The clause permits unlimited audits with no notice period and places audit costs on plan_b only when underpayment exceeds 10%, deviating from the playbook's preferred and fallback limits on audit frequency, notice, and cost allocation, thus missing critical protections.

citations.excerpt: A party may audit the other party's records relevant to this Agreement no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, at the auditing party's cost, and subject to the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement.

reviews.suggested_fallback: A party may audit the other party's records relevant to this Agreement no more than twice in any twelve (12) month period, on fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and subject to the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement. The audited party bears the cost only if the audit reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%).
reviews.verification_reason: The reviewer’s claim that the clause allows unlimited audits without notice and places audit costs on plan_b unless underpayment exceeds 10% is directly supported by the clause text. The playbook positions require limits on frequency, notice periods, and cost allocation, which the clause does not meet, so the high‑risk rating is justified. The suggested fallback text is an exact verbatim match of the playbook fallback wording. Hence the assessment is fully supported.

clause.text:
6.1 Each Party shall keep in confidence all material and information, including without limitation Content, received from the other Party and marked as confidential or which should be understood to be confidential, and may not use such material or information for any other purposes than those set forth in this Agreement. The confidentiality obligation shall, however, not be applied to material and information, which as shown by the receiving Party,

 6.1.1 is generally available or otherwise public; or

 6.1.2 the receiving Party has received from a third party without any obligation of confidentiality; or

 6.1.3 was in the possession of the receiving Party prior to receipt of the same from the other Party without any obligation of confidentiality related thereto; or

 6.1.4 the receiving party has independently developed without using material or information received from the other Party.

7 TERM OF THE AGREEMENT AND TERMINATION

clause.heading: 7 TERM OF THE AGREEMENT AND TERMINATION

reviews.rationale: The clause provides only a heading and contains no substantive language on renewal or post‑termination obligations. Consequently, the contract lacks the renewal‑opt‑in mechanism and bounded post‑termination duties required by the company's policies, creating a medium exposure as defined in the relevant positions.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term and shall renew only if both parties agree in writing to renew it. Any renewal term shall not exceed twelve (12) months.

On termination or expiry, each party's obligations cease except for those that expressly survive. Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to sixty (60) days at its then-current rates, and shall return or delete the other party's data on request.

Their risk assessment of “medium” aligns with the playbook’s “Risk if absent: medium” for both positions. The rationale distinguishes the missing clause provisions from the company’s policy requirements, and the suggested fallback verbatim matches the renewal fallback text in the playbook. All claims are properly supported.

clause.text: 7.1 Unless otherwise stated in the Appendix the term of this letter Agreement shall continue for twenty-four (24) months with the effective date unless terminated sooner or extended pursuant to the terms hereof ("Initial Term").
